auditRule: Every classification below was established by reading the current implementation on this branch. Comments, prior completion documents and PR descriptions were not accepted as evidence.

requirements.title: Persisted execution runs
requirements.currentImplementation: backend/src/ai/runStore.ts (swarm_runs, hot map + Supabase upsert, createRunDurable persists before the first provider call); backend/src/ai/executionRuntime.ts SupabaseExecutionStateStore (execution_runs).
requirements.actualBehaviour: Runs are written to Supabase and re-read on cold start via getRunAsync/listRunsForUserAsync. The execution_runs table exists in the live project with 47 rows, so the canonical-state store is not writing into a missing table.
requirements.evidence: runStore.ts:89-97 createRunDurable awaits persistToSupabase; runStore.ts:221-256 cold-start read; supabase list_tables shows public.execution_runs rows=47.
requirements.requiredChange: none
requirements.completionEvidence: runStore.ts already persisted runs before this branch; the audit classified it verified_complete and required no change.

requirements.title: Persisted executable task graphs
requirements.currentImplementation: ExecutableTaskNode[] lives inside CanonicalExecutionState.tasks and is persisted as part of the state JSON by SupabaseExecutionStateStore.
requirements.actualBehaviour: A graph can be persisted, but the only producer is executableTasksFromRoutePlan(IntelligentRoutePlan) and the main pipeline never schedules it: pipeline.ts pushes route-plan tasks into executionState and then immediately marks them completed (pipeline.ts:1027-1035) without running them.
requirements.evidence: pipeline.ts:1027 executionState.tasks.push(...executableTasksFromRoutePlan(intelligentPlan)); pipeline.ts:1030 transitionTask(..., 'completed', ...) for every non-blocked task in the same loop.
requirements.requiredChange: Produce a real implementation task graph from the plan and execute it through ExecutionScheduler instead of stamping it completed.
requirements.completionEvidence: M6 ef0d627 taskGraph.ts — buildTaskGraph persists an executable graph with explicit dependsOn edges; 32 tests in taskGraph.test.ts.

requirements.title: Dependency-aware scheduling
requirements.actualBehaviour: Ready-set computation promotes pending tasks whose dependencies all completed, blocks tasks with a terminal upstream dependency, serialises mutating tasks against read-only ones, and dedupes identical provider calls per attempt.
requirements.evidence: executionRuntime.ts:357-369.
requirements.requiredChange: none
requirements.completionEvidence: M6 taskGraphRunner.ts readyTasks/propagateBlocked schedule strictly in dependency order.

requirements.title: Restart and reconnect recovery
requirements.currentImplementation: backend/src/ai/runReconciler.ts marks orphaned swarm_runs failed on startup and fails in-flight runs on SIGTERM.
requirements.actualBehaviour: Recovery is truthful but terminal: an interrupted run is failed, never resumed. Nothing reloads a CanonicalExecutionState and continues from the last completed task.
requirements.evidence: runReconciler.ts:61-88 sets status 'error' with BUILD_INTERRUPTED; no caller of SupabaseExecutionStateStore.load exists outside tests.
requirements.requiredChange: Add resume-from-checkpoint that reloads persisted state and re-runs only unfinished tasks.
requirements.completionEvidence: M6 recoverGraph — a task found running at load was interrupted, so it resets to pending while keeping its attempt count. A crash-after-every-step loop asserts each task runs exactly once.

requirements.title: Reviewer output parsing fails closed
requirements.actualBehaviour: Unparseable and empty output correctly fall back to ok:false, so a malformed response is handled. But well-formed JSON that simply omits the ok field returns ok:true, because the expression is `parsed.ok !== false`. A reviewer that answers `{"issues":[]}` — or any object at all without an explicit ok:false — is read as a pass. That is fail-open on the exact case section 10 names: missing ok/status is not success.
requirements.evidence: qa.ts:63 `ok: parsed.ok !== false` with `ok?: boolean` optional at qa.ts:57. Also qa.ts:168 combines it as `staticResult.ok && parsed.ok && ...`, so a missing ok reaches the combined gate as true.
requirements.requiredChange: Malformed or missing status must not be success; disclose incomplete project context; name examined files and the commit SHA.
requirements.completionEvidence: M5 qa.ts — only an explicit boolean ok:true counts as a pass.

requirements.title: Reviewer must not inspect only an arbitrary first-four-file sample
requirements.actualBehaviour: Exactly the defect the command names. A fixed list of eight preferred paths is tried; if none of them exists — which is the normal case for any project that is not a Next/Expo/static scaffold at those precise paths — the reviewer is handed `files.slice(0, 4)`, the first four files in array order. Each file is truncated to 2500 characters and the whole sample to 14000, and nothing discloses to the reviewer or to the user that the review covered a fraction of the project. There is no commit SHA and no list of examined files in the reviewer's evidence.
requirements.evidence: qa.ts:93-102 fixed preferred paths; qa.ts:108 `if (!picked.length) picked.push(...files.slice(0, 4));`; qa.ts:110-112 truncation to 2500 per file and 14000 overall; no commit or file-list field on ReviewBuildOutputResult.
